mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer demand and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 5% or greater YoY decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 5% YoY for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of >5% YoY RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2% or greater YoY increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over six months signals robust manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of >2% YoY INDPRO growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point or greater increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 10% or greater YoY decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 10% YoY for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of >10% YoY HOUST decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate over one month, combined with a 0.5 percentage point or greater decline in the civilian labor force participation rate (implied from PAYEMS), signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 0.5pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2% or greater YoY increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive quarters, combined with a 1% or greater YoY increase in the Industrial Production index (INDPRO) over the same period, signals strengthening demand and supply conditions, which boost earnings and support higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 2% YoY AND INDPRO rises > 1% YoY for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of >2% YoY RSAFS AND >1% YoY INDPRO growth (t-test p > 0.05).
